lore.text: Kara Zor-El's uncle Kru-El tried to murder both her father, Zor-El, and her other uncle, Jor-El, during her name day ceremony, and her life on Krypton only got more tragic from there. Due to her father's efforts, her hometown Argo City survived the initial destruction of Krypton. Soon after, Kara's mother, Alura In-Ze, became ill and died of radiation poisoning. Kara's father realized Argo's soil was turning into Kryptonite and worked to build shields to cover every inch of ground. By the time they finished, there were only 5,000 citizens left alive. Unfortunately, the next year, an asteroid hit, penetrating the shields. Realizing they were doomed, Zor-El created a rocket large enough for a single passenger and sent his daughter out as the sole survivor. Kara landed on Earth when her cousin was early in his time as Superman. She was adopted by the Danvers family, where she grew up loved and protected, and then eventually became the protector of National City.

As a teenager, Kara lived in National City with her adoptive parents, D.E.O. agents Jeremiah and Eliza Danvers, where she attended high school while also working at the Department of Extranomal Operations under Cameron Chase. Due to her Kryptonian DNA, Earth's yellow sun gives her super senses, super-breath, flight, strength, stamina, and invulnerability. Her younger cousin Kal—who, due to her time travel in stasis in space, is now, annoyingly, her OLDER cousin— helped train her in how to harness her powers and become Supergirl. To help conceal her identity, Kara was given a special pair of glasses that darkened her blond hair to help with her cover identity as a normal civilian, Kara Danvers. Once she became an adult, Kara got an internship at media conglomerate CATCO run by Cat Grant to further balance her alter ego life with her superhero life.

Training with Superman was helpful for Kara in learning how to harness and control her yellow sun-induced powers. Unlike her cousin, she doesn't hold back as much, sometimes leading people to speculate Supergirl could be more powerful than Superman. Kara also had the chance to train in Kryptonian fighting styles like Klurkor and Torquasm Rao as a youth, which enhanced her combat abilities, but that wasn't always enough. After a battle with the Fatal Five, her powers became unstable, and Superman recommended she train under Wonder Woman's former instructor, I-Ching. I-Ching taught her Bagua and how to manipulate her Chi to regain control. Kara also trained with Batman in advanced martial arts and with the Amazons on Themyscira, mastering unarmed combat, fencing, shield work, and Amazon weapons under Wonder Woman and Artemis.

While settling into her life in National City, Kara discovered that the cyborg Zor-El she had battled before had rebuilt other deceased Kryptonians including her mother Allura and was planning to use them to help take over the Earth. Supergirl battled them and won, but her conflicted feelings for her formerly loving Kryptonian parents caused her to promise to help her father in secret. When her secret was discovered, Supergirl lost National City's trust, and Director Bones used this moment to take control of the D.E.O. and send villains to National City to try to take Supergirl out. Fortunately, Supergirl was able to defeat the villains AND win back the trust of the city she loved.

Haunted by the loss of Krypton and struggles with identity, Kara worked hard to find her place among Earth's heroes. She joined teams like the Teen Titans and the Justice League, forming close bonds with characters like Batgirl and Wonder Woman, and slowly grew into her own kind of hero, though she still sometimes struggles with forging a legacy separate from Superman's and her own feelings of isolation.

Kara's 21st birthday brought up a lot of these emotional struggles. Supergirl journeyed through space with Krypto to spend her birthday alone on a distant planet. A young girl named Ruthye approached her in a tavern and asked Supergirl to kill Krem—the man who killed Ruthye's father. Kara refused, but as she prepared to leave, Krem ambushed her, severely injuring both her and Krypto before escaping in her ship. Powerless and stranded, Kara began a reluctant journey with Ruthye. Ultimately, Kara stayed true to her morals and didn't kill Krem, but did bring him to justice. This cemented Supergirl as a flawed and deeply compassionate hero who is more than "Superman's cousin".

guide.overview: Supergirl gains **massive bonuses** from **[Superman Family] allies** present and deals **AoE Physical DMG**. She **builds up Krypton Energy** to **enhance her Ultimate**.

legacyPieces.name: House of El Symbol
legacyPieces.reason: Supergirl's signature gear. Increases Attack and grants a shield upon casting her Ultimate, improving survivability. Each Ultimate also boosts AoE damage. Paired with the stacking bonuses from [Superman Family] allies present, Supergirl's damage ramps up quickly as the battle goes on, fully showcasing the destructive force of Kryptonian Power.

legacyPieces.name: Promethium Claws
legacyPieces.reason: Provides a shield at low HP. Since Supergirl relies on powerful bonuses from [Superman Family] allies present and needs time to build up Krypton Energy, the shield keeps her alive until her damage peaks.

legacyPieces.name: Not-So-Huge Hammer
legacyPieces.reason: Increases HP, Attack, and Crit Damage. Supergirl's Ultimate damage scales with Krypton Energy, and higher base Attack and Crit Damage make her AoE burst far more devastating.

legacyPieces.name: Razor Rib Umbrella
legacyPieces.reason: Increases HP and Attack. Supergirl's survivability and damage scale with the number of [Superman Family] allies present, and the Razor Rib Umbrella's bonuses enhance this scaling.
